questions.answer_b: The accuracy of the binary system (with two digits) is higher by a factor of 5 than that of the decimal system (with 10 digits).

questions.question: How does the depletion region behave in the semiconductor diode shown here?
The following picture shows the basic structure of a semiconductor diode. How is the depletion layer formed?
questions.answer_a: At the junction, electrons migrate from the N-type side into the P-type side. This partly reduces the excess of electrons on the N-type side and partly neutralises the deficiency of electrons on the P-type side. An insulating layer forms on both sides of the boundary.
questions.answer_b: At the junction, electrons migrate from the P-type side into the N-type side. This partly reduces the excess of electrons on the P-type side and partly neutralises the deficiency of electrons on the N-type side. An insulating layer forms on both sides of the boundary.
questions.answer_c: At the junction, atoms migrate from the P-type side into the N-type side. This reduces the deficiency of atoms on the P-type side and increases the deficiency of atoms on the N-type side. A conducting layer forms on both sides of the boundary.
questions.answer_d: At the junction, atoms migrate from the N-type side into the P-type side. This reduces the deficiency of atoms on the N-type side and increases the deficiency of atoms on the P-type side. A conducting layer forms on both sides of the boundary.

questions.question: What is meant by doping?
questions.answer_a: Introducing foreign atoms of a different chemical valency into a base semiconductor material in order to provide free charge carriers.
questions.answer_b: Removing atoms from the base semiconductor material in order to reduce its electrical conductivity.
questions.answer_c: Introducing magnetic north or south poles into a base semiconductor material in order to increase its inductance.
questions.answer_d: Removing impurities from a base semiconductor material in order to generate electrons.

questions.question: What are semiconductor materials?
questions.answer_a: Some substances (e.g. silicon) are good insulators in the pure state at room temperature. However, small additions of suitable other substances (e.g. boron, phosphorus) or high temperatures turn them into conductors.
questions.answer_b: Some substances (e.g. silicon) are good conductors in the pure state at room temperature. However, small additions of suitable other substances (e.g. boron, phosphorus) or high temperatures reduce their conductivity.
questions.answer_c: Some substances (e.g. silicon) are good conductors in the pure state at room temperature. Small additions of suitable other substances (e.g. bismuth, tellurium) halve their resistance.
questions.answer_d: Some substances (e.g. silicon) are good electrolytes in the pure state at room temperature. With small additions of suitable other substances (e.g. bismuth, tellurium) they can be made into either N-type or P-type material for the anodes or cathodes of batteries.

questions.question: How does the resistance of a metal normally change with temperature?

questions.answer_b: The resistance falls as the temperature increases, i.e. the temperature coefficient is negative.
questions.answer_c: The resistance does not change as the temperature increases, i.e. the temperature coefficient is zero.
questions.answer_d: The resistance oscillates as the temperature increases, i.e. the temperature coefficient is complex.

questions.question: Which polarisations are usually distinguished in the propagation of radio waves in amateur radio, and why should they be taken into account?
questions.answer_a: A distinction is made between horizontal, vertical, and left-hand and right-hand circular polarisation. The polarisation of the transmitting and receiving antennas should be matched to ensure low-loss transmission.
questions.answer_b: A distinction is made between transverse, longitudinal and orthogonal polarisation. The polarisation of the radio must be matched to the mains to avoid short circuits.
questions.answer_c: A distinction is made between coherent, incoherent and correlated polarisation. The polarisation of the radio waves should be changed regularly to increase immunity to interference.
questions.answer_d: A distinction is made between parallel, coaxial and wireless polarisation. The polarisation of the antenna cables must be matched to the antennas to minimise losses.

questions.answer_d: I tune up my transmitter on the frequency and then start my CQ call.

questions.question: EA6VQ is calling CQ in telephony in English. Your call sign is DF1KW. How could you reply?
questions.answer_a: EA6VQ, this is DF1KW calling you.
questions.answer_b: CQ CQ CQ de DF1KW for EA6VQ, please go ahead.
questions.answer_c: EA6VQ, es ruft Sie DF1KW, bitte kommen.

questions.question: Your call sign is DH7RW. You hear an incomplete "... 7 Romeo Whiskey". How do you react?
questions.answer_a: I reply: "This is DH7RW, was I called?"
questions.answer_d: I look forward to a reply from 7R – Algeria.

questions.question: How should you reply when someone calls CQ in telephony?
questions.answer_a: I give the call sign of the calling station once, then I say once: "This is (own call sign, spelt out), over".
questions.answer_b: I give the call sign of the calling station at least five times, and then I say at least once: "This is (own call sign, spelt out)".
questions.answer_c: I also call CQ and give the call sign of the calling station at least three times, then I say at least five times: "This is (own call sign, spelt out)".
questions.answer_d: I give my call sign and ask the calling station to continue calling on another frequency (at least twice).

questions.question: How can you start an amateur radio contact, for example?
questions.answer_a: By using the international operating abbreviation CQ, that is, with a general call; with a directed call to a particular station; or with a reply to a general call, in each case giving your own call sign.
questions.answer_b: By repeatedly sending the international Q code "QRZ?" followed by your own call sign, and listening on the frequency in the pauses between transmissions.
questions.answer_c: By sending the abbreviation CQ, your own call sign and the Q code "QTH" several times (often, when propagation conditions are poor), listening in between.
questions.answer_d: By sending your call sign and the 1750 Hz tone burst laid down by the IARU, from which listening stations recognise that you want a contact.

questions.question: How do you give the other station its "report" in SSTV?
questions.answer_a: I write the report directly into the picture to be transmitted.
questions.answer_b: I give the report later on the QSL card.
questions.answer_c: I send the report in CW after the picture transmission.
questions.answer_d: I give the report in SSB during the picture transmission.

questions.answer_a: Readability on a scale of 1 to 5, signal strength on a scale of 1 to 9 and tone on a scale of 1 to 9
questions.answer_b: Readability on a scale of 1 to 5, signal strength on a scale of 1 to 5 and pitch on a scale of 1 to 9
questions.answer_c: Signal quality on a scale of 1 to 5, signal strength on a scale of 1 to 5 and tone on a scale of 1 to 9
questions.answer_d: Readability on a scale of 1 to 9, signal quality on a scale of 1 to 5 and pitch on a scale of 1 to 4

questions.question: The reception quality of a transmission can be assessed with the letters RST. What do they stand for?
questions.answer_a: R = readability, S = signal strength, T = tone
questions.answer_b: R = radio call sign, S = signal strength, T = tone
questions.answer_c: R = readability, S = signal strength, T = transmit frequency

questions.question: What is meant by the RST report? It is a short code ...
questions.answer_c: for describing the state of the ionosphere.

sections.title: Contests, pile-ups, DXpeditions and direction finding (ARDF)

questions.question: What do radio amateurs mean by a "foxhunt" (ARDF = Amateur Radio Direction Finding)?
questions.answer_a: It is a radio direction-finding competition in which small hidden transmitters in the HF or VHF range, which transmit only briefly, have to be found with portable direction-finding receivers.
questions.answer_b: It is a radio competition in which the aim is to make contacts with as many countries as possible on one amateur band within a given time.
questions.answer_c: In a foxhunt the aim is to follow the path of small mobile transmitters and to recognise a pattern in it.
questions.answer_d: It is a radio direction-finding competition that radio amateurs organise exclusively for SWLs (short-wave listeners).

questions.question: What is meant by a "DXpedition" in amateur radio?
questions.answer_a: It is an amateur radio expedition to countries or islands that are rarely heard in amateur radio.
questions.answer_b: It is a worldwide activity week.
questions.answer_c: It is an international radio contest.
questions.answer_d: It is a list of all the countries still sought after by radio amateurs.

questions.question: A station that has been calling CQ on 14205 kHz says at the end of its call "tuning 290 to 300 up". Which frequencies do you use if you want to call this station?
questions.answer_a: I call between 14290 and 14300 kHz and listen on 14205 kHz.
questions.answer_b: I call and listen between 14290 and 14300 kHz.
questions.answer_c: I call on 14205 kHz and listen between 14290 and 14300 kHz.
questions.answer_d: I call on 14290 kHz and listen on 14300 kHz.

questions.question: At the end of its CQ call a station sends "5 up". What does this mean, and what must be observed?
questions.answer_a: The calling station is listening 5 kHz above its own transmit frequency. So when I call, I must transmit 5 kHz higher.
questions.answer_b: The calling station will listen on its own transmit frequency 5 minutes later. So I must call 5 minutes later and check beforehand that the frequency is free.
questions.answer_c: The calling station transmits 5 kHz above its own transmit frequency. So when I call, I must receive 5 kHz higher and check beforehand that the frequency is free.
questions.answer_d: The calling station will deal with my call in 5th place. So when I call, I must wait for 4 other contacts.

questions.question: What does it mean when a sought-after station calls CQ and ends the call with "split up 14270 to 14280"? The station ...
questions.answer_a: is listening above its transmit frequency on varying frequencies within the range given.
questions.answer_b: is announcing a change of its transmit frequency to the range given.
questions.answer_c: is asking calling stations to use CW in the range given.
questions.answer_d: will transmit in the range given with a bandwidth of 10 kHz.

questions.question: What is "split operation"?
questions.answer_a: Transmitting and receiving on different frequencies
questions.answer_c: Sharing a frequency between two repeaters
questions.answer_d: Using different transmission modes in one QSO

questions.question: What do you understand by a rare station's request for "list operation"?
questions.answer_a: Another station that can be heard well puts calling stations on a list and later calls these stations to make a contact with the rare station.
questions.answer_b: Another station that can be heard well sends lists of calling stations to the rare station via the internet.
questions.answer_c: The rare station calls stations in alphabetical order from a list of country prefixes.
questions.answer_d: The rare station or its QSL manager publishes a list of the stations worked, in the amateur radio magazines.

questions.question: A sought-after station calls in telephony "only number 3". What does this mean? The station ...
questions.answer_a: wants calls from stations with the digit 3 between prefix and suffix.
questions.answer_b: wants to put three calling stations on a list at a time.
questions.answer_c: wants to call stations with a three-letter suffix.
questions.answer_d: wants calling stations to give their suffix three times.

questions.question: What is meant by the term "pile-up"? In amateur radio it means the simultaneous ...
questions.answer_a: calling of a sought-after station by many amateur stations.
questions.answer_b: transmission by one station on several amateur frequencies.
questions.answer_c: direction finding of a station with several directional antennas stacked one above the other.
questions.answer_d: reception of a station by many remote stations during a contest.

questions.question: Which special rule applies in a "sprint contest"?
questions.answer_a: After each contact, the station that called CQ leaves the frequency to the other station.
questions.answer_b: Operation is in telegraphy, and the sending speed counts towards the score.
questions.answer_c: The call sign must not be spelt out, except at the beginning and at the end of the contest.
questions.answer_d: Participants must keep constantly on the move while operating.

questions.question: You are taking part in an amateur radio contest. What information should you exchange in a QSO?
questions.answer_a: I pass on the data laid down in the contest rules, so that the contact counts.
questions.answer_b: I send call sign, signal report, name, location and a description of my station, so that the other station's log is complete.
questions.answer_c: I decide for each contact which data I send, so that I do not give away too much about myself.
questions.answer_d: I limit myself to the call sign, so that I can make as many contacts as possible quickly.

questions.question: Why is the exchange of information in contacts during an amateur radio contest particularly short?
questions.answer_a: To make as many contacts as possible in the given time.
questions.answer_b: To keep to the time limit set for a single contact.
questions.answer_c: Because there is otherwise a risk of disqualification.
questions.answer_d: Because all the necessary information can also be found on the internet.

questions.question: What is the purpose of an amateur radio contest? It is for competing and for ...
questions.answer_a: the continuous improvement of amateur radio equipment and operating technique.
questions.answer_d: testing the immunity of the neighbours' receiving equipment.

questions.question: What is the transponder of an "OSCAR", and how does it work?
questions.answer_a: It is a converter on board an amateur satellite which converts the received signals to another frequency range and transmits them back to earth.
questions.answer_b: It is a stratospheric balloon carrying a remotely controlled amateur station, which processes received signals and transmits them back to earth.
questions.answer_c: It is a converter on board an amateur satellite which automatically transmits the weather pictures recorded by the satellite and other telemetry data to earth.
questions.answer_d: It is a beacon transmitter on board an amateur satellite, used for observing propagation conditions in the VHF, UHF and SHF ranges.

questions.question: What does the abbreviation OSCAR stand for in amateur radio?
What does the term elevation mean in satellite communication?
questions.answer_c: Direction of transmission from the satellite to earth
questions.answer_d: Direction of transmission from earth to the satellite

questions.question: What does the term azimuth mean in satellite communication?
questions.answer_c: Direction of transmission from the satellite to earth
questions.answer_d: Direction of transmission from earth to the satellite

questions.question: What does the term downlink mean in satellite communication?
questions.answer_a: Direction of transmission from the satellite to earth
questions.answer_b: Direction of transmission from earth to the satellite

questions.question: What does the term uplink mean in satellite communication?
questions.answer_a: Direction of transmission from earth to the satellite
questions.answer_b: Direction of transmission from the satellite to earth

questions.question: Why should the frequencies 14099 to 14101 kHz, 18109 to 18111 kHz, 21149 to 21151 kHz, 24929 to 24931 kHz and 28190 to 28225 kHz be kept clear?
questions.answer_a: Under the IARU recommendation, these frequencies are intended for the International Beacon Project (IBP) and are to be kept clear for observing propagation conditions by means of beacon signals.
questions.answer_b: Under the IARU recommendation, these frequency ranges are intended for HAMNET and should be kept clear for monitoring these transmissions.
questions.answer_c: Under the IARU recommendation, these frequencies are intended especially for DX traffic and should preferably be used for contacts during "DX expeditions".
questions.answer_d: Under a recommendation of the Radio Regulations (RR), these frequency ranges are intended for special amateur standard-frequency and time-signal transmissions and should be kept clear as far as possible.

questions.question: What is a common use of amateur radio beacons? They ...
questions.answer_b: reserve frequencies for a radio amateur.
questions.answer_c: post reception reports on the internet.
questions.answer_d: ionise the D region of the atmosphere.

questions.question: How is a contact assessed when working through a repeater?
questions.answer_a: Only the readability "R" is assessed, because the signal strength "S" relates to the repeater.
questions.answer_b: The readability "R" and the signal strength "S" are assessed, because both are part of a complete report.
questions.answer_c: Only the signal strength "S" is assessed, because the readability "R" is always equally good with a repeater.
questions.answer_d: Only verbal statements are made, as an exact assessment is not possible when operating through a repeater.

questions.question: Why should you make sure that your handheld is set to narrowband FM when using an FM repeater? Because otherwise ...
questions.answer_a: repeater inputs on adjacent frequencies may suffer interference, and the repeater in use could put out a distorted signal.
questions.answer_b: excessive wear of the repeater's preamplifier could occur through overload, and the repeater would then fail.
questions.answer_c: excessive harmonics may be generated, and radio services on other bands could suffer interference from image frequencies.
questions.answer_d: the batteries of the repeater's emergency power supply could be excessively loaded and would then no longer be usable in an emergency.

questions.question: Why should overs be kept as short as possible when operating through repeaters?
questions.answer_a: So that mobile and portable stations in particular can use the repeater more easily.
questions.answer_b: To allow simplex operation from time to time.
questions.answer_c: Under the Amateur Radio Ordinance (Amateurfunkverordnung, AFuV), an over may last no more than 60 seconds.
questions.answer_d: The voice memories of a repeater have a limited capacity.

questions.question: How should simultaneous talking (doubling) be avoided when using a repeater and in nets?
questions.answer_a: By a proper handover after each over
questions.answer_c: By transmitting with as much power as possible
questions.answer_d: By slightly detuning the transmit frequency

questions.question: How should it be made easier for stations to join a net in progress or a conversation on a repeater?
questions.answer_a: By a short pause before each over
questions.answer_c: By keeping the input frequency clear
questions.answer_d: By keeping the output frequency clear

questions.question: At German 70 cm repeaters, the input frequency is usually ...
questions.answer_a: 7.6 MHz lower than the output frequency.
questions.answer_b: 600 kHz higher than the output frequency.
questions.answer_c: 600 kHz lower than the output frequency.
questions.answer_d: 7.6 MHz higher than the output frequency.

questions.question: At German 2 m repeaters, the input frequency is usually ...
questions.answer_a: 600 kHz lower than the output frequency.
questions.answer_b: 600 kHz higher than the output frequency.
questions.answer_c: 7.6 MHz lower than the output frequency.
questions.answer_d: 7.6 MHz higher than the output frequency.

questions.question: What is meant when it is said that a repeater has an input and an output frequency?
questions.answer_a: The repeater receives on the input frequency and transmits on the output frequency.
questions.answer_b: When the input frequency is heavily occupied, the repeater provides an additional output frequency.
questions.answer_c: The repeater uses an input frequency for converting the received signal and the output frequency for remote control.
questions.answer_d: The repeater must be opened with a tone call on the output frequency before it can go into operation on the input frequency.

sections.title: Emergency communications and message handling in natural disasters

questions.question: According to the recommendations of the International Amateur Radio Union (IARU), there are so-called centres of activity for emergency communications at 3760, 7110, 14300, 18160 and 21360 kHz. What is special about these frequencies? They are to ...
questions.answer_a: serve emergency communications in ITU Region 1 and be kept clear for them.
questions.answer_b: be monitored permanently, provided the radio has a 2nd VFO.
questions.answer_c: serve exclusively for use by the rescue services and not be used by radio amateurs.
questions.answer_d: be used only after prior announcement by the IARU.

questions.question: On 16 August (local date) at 20:00 Central European Summer Time (CEST), you received an emergency message from 9J2NG and passed it on by telephone to a relief organisation. The amateur station 9J2NG has asked you to contact it again at 23:00 UTC. What time is this in Germany?
You have answered a distress message and informed the police or the emergency control centre. What is the exemplary thing to do next?
questions.answer_a: I remain reachable and pass on information until help has arrived.
questions.answer_b: I call the police or the emergency control centre regularly to ask about progress.
questions.answer_c: I switch off my radio, as I have done my duty.
questions.answer_d: I inform the media so that the rescue operation can be reported live.

questions.question: You have received a distress message. No other station responds, and you could help. What do you do?
questions.answer_a: I answer the call and inform the police or the emergency control centre.
questions.answer_b: I switch off my radio so as not to get into trouble.
questions.answer_c: I immediately repeat the distress message on the same frequency.
questions.answer_d: I wait about an hour to see whether a rescue organisation responds.

questions.question: You have received a distress message, which is answered after a short time by a rescue organisation. What do you do?
questions.answer_a: I do not disrupt the radio traffic under any circumstances.
questions.answer_b: I offer my help between two overs.
questions.answer_c: I tune up my transmitter on the frequency.
questions.answer_d: I ask as many radio amateurs as possible for help.

questions.question: You hear a distress message. What do you do first?
questions.answer_a: I listen carefully and note down all important information.
questions.answer_b: I send MAYDAY three times and my call sign, and wait for a reply.
questions.answer_c: I tune up my transmitter on the frequency.
questions.answer_d: I change frequency or switch off.

questions.question: You come to the scene of an accident. The first-aider asks you to summon help via your mobile amateur station, as the mobile phone network is not available. What do you do?
questions.answer_a: I call a radio amateur by radio and ask them to inform the police or the emergency control centre.
questions.answer_b: I refuse to help, since no information for third parties may be passed in amateur radio.
questions.answer_c: I call MAYDAY by radio at least three times, followed by my call sign, the location and the nature of the emergency.
questions.answer_d: I refuse to help, since no distress signals may be used in amateur radio.

questions.question: Are you permitted to use SOS or MAYDAY within amateur radio in an emergency?
questions.answer_b: Not MAYDAY, but SOS in an emergency.
questions.answer_d: Not SOS, but MAYDAY in an emergency.

questions.question: What are the international distress signals outside amateur radio?
Which alternatives to the QSL card are common? Confirmation of contacts by ...
questions.answer_a: electronic QSL cards or log upload
questions.answer_b: the BNetzA as an independent body
questions.answer_c: the Intruder Watch of the amateur radio societies
questions.answer_d: certification by a notary or an SWL specialist lawyer

questions.question: Where can you find the addresses of foreign radio amateurs to whom you want to send your QSL card direct?
questions.answer_a: I find them in the international amateur radio call sign list (callbook) or from information on the internet.
questions.answer_b: I find them in the amateur radio call sign list on the website of the Federal Network Agency (BNetzA).
questions.answer_c: I find them in the Radio Regulations (RR).
questions.answer_d: I find them in the international telephone directory.

questions.question: HZ1HZ told you "QSL via K8PYD". What would you do to receive the QSL card from HZ1HZ?
questions.answer_a: I send my QSL card via K8PYD, because that station is the QSL manager of HZ1HZ.
questions.answer_b: I must send my QSL card via HZ1HZ, because K8PYD was the other station in the QSO.
questions.answer_c: I look up the address of HZ1HZ in the callbook and send the card direct.
questions.answer_d: I wait until HZ1HZ has sent the card to K8PYD.

questions.question: What time do you enter on the QSL card if you had a contact at 13:30 CEST?
What time do you enter on the QSL card if you had a QSO at 15:30 CET?
What should you bear in mind when entering times on QSL cards? They should be entered in ...
questions.answer_a: Coordinated Universal Time (UTC), to make it easier for other stations abroad to find the contact in their log.
questions.answer_b: your own local time, to comply with German regulations.
questions.answer_c: the local time of the other station, so that there is no confusion.
questions.answer_d: your own local time and also in the local time of the other station, both to comply with German regulations and to make it easier for other stations abroad to find the contact in their log.

questions.question: What information should QSL cards contain <u>as a minimum</u>?
questions.answer_a: Call sign used, call sign of the other station, date and time of the contact in UTC, band, mode and signal report
questions.answer_b: Call sign used, date and time of the contact in UTC, frequency, mode, signal report, as well as your own name, location, locator, your own transmitter power and details of the technical equipment used
questions.answer_c: Call sign of the other station, date and time of the contact in UTC, exact frequency, mode, signal report and other usual details such as your own name, location, locator and your own transmitter power
questions.answer_d: Call sign of the other station, date and time of the contact in UTC, frequency, mode, details of the propagation conditions and the operator's signature

questions.question: A QSL card is ...
questions.answer_a: the confirmation of an amateur radio contact. It serves, for example, as proof when applying for amateur radio awards.
questions.answer_b: the certificate of membership of an amateur radio society.
questions.answer_c: a map on which the locations for fixed-location radio contests are marked.
questions.answer_d: a reservation confirmation for taking part in an amateur radio net. It secures the radio amateur a place on the list in the net.

questions.question: When keeping a log has been ordered, what must be taken into account when changing the "logging software"?
questions.answer_a: The log data must remain available, so that the operating data can be inspected in any later checks.
questions.answer_b: You should change to software for a 64-bit system.
questions.answer_c: The old software must always be deleted, to avoid conflicts between data formats.
questions.answer_d: You should use a logging program that allows the data to be stored in the cloud.

questions.question: When keeping a log has been ordered, what must be observed when creating a "computer log"?
questions.answer_a: As with a paper log, the data must be available for inspection for a certain period.
questions.answer_b: The log file must also be readable with a word processor.
questions.answer_c: A conventional paper log must be kept as well.
questions.answer_d: A printout of the log must be available at all times.

questions.question: What do radio amateurs mean by a log?
questions.answer_a: It is the station log that a radio amateur keeps voluntarily or must keep in special cases.
questions.answer_b: It is the station log that every radio amateur must keep.
questions.answer_c: It is the documentation of all the radio amateur's equipment and antennas.
questions.answer_d: It is the documentation of compliance with the safety distances for the protection of persons.

sections.title: Examination questions in the examination part: Knowledge of regulations
Definition of the amateur service and the amateur-satellite service

questions.question: What does the definition of the amateur service in the Radio Regulations (RR) say about radio amateurs?
questions.answer_a: Radio amateurs are duly authorised persons interested in radio technique solely with a personal aim and without pecuniary interest.
questions.answer_b: Nothing, since the amateur service is not defined in the Radio Regulations (RR).
questions.answer_c: Radio amateurs are holders of an examination certificate who are concerned with radio technique for commercial purposes.
questions.answer_d: Radio amateurs may only transmit messages of minor importance, for which recourse to public telecommunications services is not justified.

questions.question: According to the definition in the Radio Regulations (RR), what is the amateur-satellite service for?
questions.answer_a: For the same purposes as the rest of the amateur service
questions.answer_b: For observing terrestrial weather in the X-ray spectrum
questions.answer_c: For determining the attenuation of the ionising regions
questions.answer_d: For determining the attenuation of the reflecting layers in the UHF range

questions.question: According to the definition in the Radio Regulations (RR), what is the amateur service for?
questions.answer_a: For self-training, for intercommunication between radio amateurs and for technical investigations
questions.answer_b: For communication between radio amateurs and with other radiocommunication services
questions.answer_c: For providing communication services in areas that lack communication infrastructure
questions.answer_d: For communication between radio amateurs and their family and friends

questions.question: In which international set of rules is the term "amateur service" defined?
questions.answer_a: In the Radio Regulations (RR) of the ITU
questions.answer_b: In the standards and recommendations of ETSI
questions.answer_c: In the recommendations of the IARU
questions.answer_d: In the provisions of the CEPT

questions.question: How is the "amateur station" defined in the Radio Regulations (RR)? An amateur station is ...
questions.answer_a: a station in the amateur service.
questions.answer_b: a station operated by radio amateurs.
questions.answer_c: a station that transmits on amateur frequencies.
questions.answer_d: a station with a call sign.

questions.question: In essence, how is a station defined in the Radio Regulations (RR)?
questions.answer_a: A station consists of transmitters, receivers or transceivers and the accessory equipment necessary at one location for operation.
questions.answer_b: The term station is not defined in the Radio Regulations (RR).
questions.answer_c: A station consists of transmitters, receivers or transceivers without accessory equipment.
questions.answer_d: A station consists of at least one transceiver and an antenna, including the person operating them.

questions.question: What do the Radio Regulations (RR) lay down regarding the Morse qualification of radio amateurs?
questions.answer_a: The national administration of each country decides independently whether a Morse test is required.
questions.answer_b: With a transmitter power of more than 100 W, a radio amateur needs proof of having passed a Morse test.
questions.answer_c: Anyone who wants to use frequencies below 30 MHz must pass a Morse test.
questions.answer_d: The Radio Regulations (RR) contain no provisions on the Morse qualification.

questions.question: Under the Radio Regulations (RR), what content in international amateur radio communication may be encoded for the purpose of obscuring its meaning?
questions.answer_a: Control signals between earth command stations and amateur satellites
questions.answer_b: Confidential information and remarks of a personal character
questions.answer_c: Content that is digitally encoded because of the transmission method used
questions.answer_d: Content concerning technical matters of the amateur service that are worth protecting

questions.question: What do the Radio Regulations (RR) lay down regarding amateur radio communication?
questions.answer_a: Communication between amateur stations of different countries shall be limited to communications incidental to the purpose of the amateur service as defined and to remarks of a personal character.
questions.answer_b: Amateur stations are not permitted to take part in the radio traffic of emergency and disaster communication exercises.
questions.answer_c: It must be ensured that communication between amateur stations is not made accessible to third parties.
questions.answer_d: The content of messages in cross-border amateur radio communication shall be limited to purely technical content.

questions.question: The general provisions of the Radio Regulations (RR) apply ...
questions.answer_a: to the amateur service as well.
questions.answer_c: only as regards laying down the frequency bands for the amateur service.
questions.answer_d: only as regards laying down the classes of emission for the amateur service.

questions.question: In which international set of rules can the meanings of the Q codes used in amateur radio be looked up? In the ...
questions.answer_b: recommendations of the International Amateur Radio Union (IARU)
questions.answer_c: standards of the European Telecommunications Standards Institute (ETSI)
questions.answer_d: recommendations of the International Organization for Standardization (ISO)

questions.question: Where are the prefixes for amateur call signs regulated internationally?
questions.answer_b: In the Amateur Radio Act (Amateurfunkgesetz, AFuG)
questions.answer_c: In the call sign list of the BNetzA
questions.answer_d: In the Amateur Radio Ordinance (Amateurfunkverordnung, AFuV)

questions.question: To which region under the Radio Regulations (RR) does Australia belong?
To which region under the Radio Regulations (RR) does Canada belong?
To which region under the Radio Regulations (RR) does Germany belong?
Under the Radio Regulations (RR), the world is divided into regions for the allocation of frequency bands to radiocommunication services. How many regions are there?
Why do the Radio Regulations (RR) divide the earth into different regions?
questions.answer_a: To be able to make different allocations of frequency bands to the radiocommunication services in the regions
questions.answer_b: Because amateur radio communication is permitted only within one region
questions.answer_c: To be able to introduce rules on guest licences for the individual regions
questions.answer_d: Because they are different time zones, and this simplifies radio communication

sections.title: CEPT provisions (European Conference of Postal and Telecommunications Administrations)

questions.question: Is temporary operation of a German club station under CEPT Recommendation T/R 61-01 permitted in a country that applies this recommendation?
questions.answer_a: No, operating a club station requires an application for a guest licence.
questions.answer_b: Yes, but only if the club station is not operated at a fixed location abroad.
questions.answer_c: Yes, operating a club station is permitted if the planned location abroad has been notified beforehand to the competent regional office of the Federal Network Agency (BNetzA).
questions.answer_d: No, because there are no club stations in the other CEPT countries.

questions.question: What must a radio amateur do to operate an amateur station in a country that does not apply the CEPT recommendation?
questions.answer_a: Apply for a guest licence to the competent authority of that country.
questions.answer_b: Obtain a special permit from the Federal Network Agency (BNetzA).
questions.answer_c: Nothing, if the host country applies the IARU recommendations.
questions.answer_d: Nothing, since temporary operation is permitted under reciprocal agreements.

questions.question: May a radio amateur with a German amateur radio licence also operate on the 6 m band abroad?
questions.answer_a: The radio amateur must comply with the provisions of the host country within the scope of the CEPT radio amateur licence.
questions.answer_b: The permission to operate on the 6 m band must be shown in the amateur radio licence.
questions.answer_c: To do so, the radio amateur must apply for a CEPT radio amateur licence in the host country.
questions.answer_d: Operation on the 6 m band is not permitted abroad.

questions.question: Which provisions must be observed when operating an amateur station abroad if the country visited has implemented CEPT Recommendations T/R 61-01 and (05)06?
questions.answer_a: The applicable CEPT recommendation and the provisions and conditions in force in the host country. Transmitter power, for example, must be adapted to the provisions of the host country.
questions.answer_b: The provisions of the host country, but only if the radio amateur is staying there permanently. Stations operated as mobile stations (e.g. when passing through) can be used as in Germany.
questions.answer_c: The applicable CEPT recommendation and the provisions and conditions in force in the home country. Transmitter power, for example, need not be adapted to the provisions of the host country.
questions.answer_d: In countries of the European Union (EU) the same laws apply as in Germany. Outside the EU, the national laws of each country must be observed.

questions.question: How must a radio amateur from a country that applies CEPT Recommendation T/R 61-01 or ECC Recommendation (05)06 supplement the home call sign when operating an amateur station in Germany? Depending on the radio amateur's class, ...
For how long per stay may a radio amateur carry out temporary amateur radio operation abroad if the CEPT arrangement applies?
May a radio amateur with a German Class A or E authorisation to participate in the amateur service also operate in non-CEPT countries on the basis of CEPT Recommendation T/R 61-01 or ECC (05)06?
questions.answer_a: Yes, if these countries apply the relevant CEPT recommendation.
questions.answer_b: Yes, worldwide, since the ITU has declared the CEPT recommendations to be generally applicable.
questions.answer_c: No, the application of the CEPT recommendations is reserved for members of the CEPT.
questions.answer_d: No, the German amateur radio licence is restricted to members of the CEPT.

questions.question: May a German radio amateur with a Class A amateur radio licence operate in all CEPT countries?
questions.answer_a: No, only in the countries that have implemented Recommendation T/R 61-01, provided the radio amateur has no permanent residence there.
questions.answer_b: Yes, all CEPT member countries must apply Recommendation T/R 61-01.
questions.answer_c: No, CEPT Recommendation T/R 61-01 may be applied only in the member states of the European Union.
questions.answer_d: Yes, but the amateur radio rules of the home country must be followed.

questions.question: May a radio amateur with a "CEPT Novice Radio Amateur Licence" operate in all CEPT countries?
questions.answer_a: No, only in countries that have implemented ECC Recommendation (05)06, provided the radio amateur has no permanent residence there.
questions.answer_b: Yes, all CEPT member countries must apply ECC Recommendation (05)06.
questions.answer_c: No, ECC Recommendation (05)06 may be applied only in the member states of the European Union.
questions.answer_d: Yes, but the amateur radio rules of the home country must be followed.

questions.question: May a radio amateur with a Class N amateur radio licence operate in all CEPT countries?
questions.answer_a: No, licence class N is valid only in Germany.
questions.answer_b: No, licence class N is valid only within the European Union.
questions.answer_c: Yes, operation in all CEPT countries is permitted if the radio amateur complies with the provisions of the home country.
questions.answer_d: Yes, operation in all CEPT countries is permitted if the radio amateur complies with the provisions of the host country.

questions.question: What significance do CEPT Recommendations T/R 61-01 and T/R 61-02, ERC Report 32 and ECC Recommendation (05)06 have for amateur radio? They form the basis for ...
questions.answer_a: temporary amateur radio operation and the mutual recognition of amateur radio certificates in the implementing countries.
questions.answer_b: radio communication between the implementing countries and the harmonisation of national frequency allocations for the amateur service.
questions.answer_c: amateur radio communication in the implementing countries and the worldwide recognition of amateur radio certificates.
questions.answer_d: the cross-border movement of amateur radio equipment in the European Union and other implementing countries.

questions.question: What is a HAREC certificate? The document ...
questions.answer_a: certifies that a Class A examination has been passed in accordance with CEPT Recommendation T/R 61-02. With it, a radio amateur can obtain an amateur radio licence in the participating countries.
questions.answer_b: entitles the radio amateur to carry out temporary amateur radio operation under CEPT Recommendation T/R 61-01.
questions.answer_c: certifies that a Class E examination has been passed in accordance with ECC (05)06. With it, a radio amateur can obtain an amateur radio licence in the participating countries.
questions.answer_d: is issued to radio amateurs who have passed the voluntary Morse test.

questions.question: What is meant by the term HAREC (Harmonised Amateur Radio Examination Certificate)?
questions.answer_a: It is a harmonised amateur radio examination certificate in accordance with CEPT Recommendation T/R 61-02. The Class A amateur radio certificate corresponds to this recommendation.
questions.answer_b: It is a harmonised CEPT radio amateur licence in accordance with CEPT Recommendation T/R 61-01.
questions.answer_c: It is a harmonised CEPT Novice Radio Amateur Examination Certificate in accordance with ERC Report 32. The Class E amateur radio certificate corresponds to this recommendation.
questions.answer_d: It is a harmonised CEPT Novice Radio Amateur Licence in accordance with ECC Recommendation (05)06.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the "CEPT Novice Radio Amateur Examination Certificate" is correct?
questions.answer_a: It can simplify the issue of a corresponding individual novice licence for radio amateurs in another country.
questions.answer_b: It entitles the holder to carry out amateur radio operation abroad under the German provisions.
questions.answer_c: It entitles the holder to carry out amateur radio operation under CEPT Recommendation T/R 61-01.
questions.answer_d: Holders of the CEPT Novice Radio Amateur Examination Certificate are generally not permitted to carry out amateur radio operation abroad.

questions.question: What must a radio amateur who commits an administrative offence when operating an amateur station expect?
questions.answer_a: The Federal Network Agency (BNetzA) can punish the offence with a fine.
questions.answer_b: The radio amateur must expect the amateur radio certificate to be withdrawn.
questions.answer_c: The radio amateur must expect the amateur radio installation to be seized by the BNetzA.
questions.answer_d: The Federal Network Agency (BNetzA) can order a re-examination subject to a fee.

questions.question: Which of the following acts are administrative offences within the meaning of the Amateur Radio Act (Amateurfunkgesetz, AFuG) and can be punished with fines of up to 5000 or 10000 euros?
questions.answer_a: (1) Operation without a licence and without the assignment of a call sign; (2) Providing telecommunications services on a commercial basis; (3) Passing messages to third parties
questions.answer_b: (1) Exceeding the permitted transmit power; (2) Permanently moving the amateur station to another location; (3) Operating without carrying the licence document
questions.answer_c: (1) Giving the call sign inadequately; (2) Exceeding the permitted bandwidth of an emission; (3) Simultaneous use of one call sign from different locations
questions.answer_d: (1) Encrypting amateur radio communication to obscure its content; (2) Operating a remote station without an operating notification; (3) Letting third parties use the call sign

questions.question: What must a radio amateur with an assigned call sign expect in the event of continued violations of the AFuG or AFuV?
questions.answer_a: Revocation of the amateur radio licence
questions.answer_c: A re-examination subject to a fee
questions.answer_d: Confiscation of the amateur radio certificate

questions.question: In the event of violations of the AFuG or AFuV, the Federal Network Agency (BNetzA) can ...
questions.answer_a: order operation to be restricted or the amateur station to be taken out of service.
questions.answer_b: order the amateur station to be dismantled immediately, on the spot.
questions.answer_c: order the amateur station to be rendered unusable by removing important parts from the transmitter.
questions.answer_d: order a re-examination of competence subject to a fee.

questions.question: Under the Amateur Radio Act (Amateurfunkgesetz, AFuG), can a radio amateur obtain a site certificate?
questions.answer_a: The BNetzA issues a site certificate on application.
questions.answer_b: The radio amateur cannot obtain a site certificate from the BNetzA, even on application.
questions.answer_c: The site certificate can be produced with the IT application "Watt-Wächter".
questions.answer_d: The BNetzA issues a site certificate when it assigns the call sign.

questions.question: In the case of home-built equipment, may a radio amateur deviate from the essential requirements on immunity within the meaning of the Act on the Electromagnetic Compatibility of Equipment (EMVG)?
questions.answer_a: Yes, radio amateurs can determine the degree of immunity of their equipment themselves.
questions.answer_b: Yes, but only in the direction of improving immunity
questions.answer_c: No, the immunity is specified and must be complied with.
questions.answer_d: No, with regard to immunity, home-built amateur radio equipment must match commercially manufactured equipment.

questions.question: What applies regarding the immunity of the amateur station according to the wording of the Amateur Radio Act (Amateurfunkgesetz, AFuG)?
questions.answer_a: The radio amateur may deviate from the essential requirements under the Act on the Electromagnetic Compatibility of Equipment (EMVG) and can personally determine the degree of immunity of the amateur station.
questions.answer_b: The radio amateur must have the amateur station undergo an immunity test by the BNetzA every 2 years.
questions.answer_c: With regard to their immunity, amateur stations are treated in the same way as other equipment.
questions.answer_d: Amateur stations must accept electromagnetic interference from other equipment even if that equipment does not meet the essential requirements under the Act on the Electromagnetic Compatibility of Equipment (EMVG).

questions.question: What must a radio amateur observe with regard to electromagnetic compatibility when operating an amateur station?
questions.answer_a: The radio amateur must comply with the protection requirements for ensuring electromagnetic compatibility within the meaning of the Act on the Electromagnetic Compatibility of Equipment (EMVG).
questions.answer_b: The radio amateur needs a current compatibility certificate from the BNetzA for the amateur station.
questions.answer_c: The amateur station may consist only of type-tested radio equipment that meets the requirements of the Act on Radio Equipment (FuAG).
questions.answer_d: The amateur station must be checked for compliance with electromagnetic compatibility by a certified master electrician. The acceptance report must be kept available for the BNetzA.

questions.question: Can an assigned call sign be changed by the Federal Network Agency (BNetzA)?
questions.answer_a: The call sign can be changed for important reasons, in particular when international requirements change.
questions.answer_b: On moving into the area of responsibility of another regional office of the Federal Network Agency (BNetzA), the radio amateur receives a new call sign assignment.
questions.answer_c: The assigned call sign is the property of the radio amateur and is not changed by the Federal Network Agency (BNetzA).
questions.answer_d: If the notification under the Ordinance on the Verification Procedure for Limiting Electromagnetic Fields (BEMFV) changes, the radio amateur receives a different call sign.

questions.question: Which personal call signs may a radio amateur use?
questions.answer_a: Only a call sign that the Federal Network Agency (BNetzA) has assigned to that radio amateur
questions.answer_c: Only a call sign assigned by an amateur radio society
questions.answer_d: When using another person's station, the personal call sign of the station holder

questions.question: For what purpose may an amateur station <u>not</u> be operated under the Amateur Radio Act (Amateurfunkgesetz, AFuG)?
questions.answer_a: For providing telecommunications services on a commercial basis

questions.question: May the amateur station be operated for commercial purposes? An amateur station may ...
questions.answer_a: not be operated for commercial purposes.
questions.answer_b: be operated for commercial purposes once the business has been registered, stating the call sign.
questions.answer_c: be operated for the purpose of providing telecommunications services on a commercial basis.
questions.answer_d: be operated for commercial purposes after approval by the Federal Network Agency (BNetzA).

questions.question: Under the Amateur Radio Act (Amateurfunkgesetz, AFuG), a radio amateur is the holder of an amateur radio certificate or a harmonised examination certificate who is concerned with the amateur service out of personal interest and <u>not</u> ...
questions.answer_b: out of political or religious interest.
questions.answer_d: out of social or cultural interest.

questions.question: May a radio amateur transmit messages that do not concern the amateur service on behalf of and to third parties?
questions.answer_d: Only when requested by the competent regional office of the Federal Network Agency (BNetzA)

questions.question: With which stations may a radio amateur carry on radio communication?
questions.answer_b: With all stations active on the amateur bands
questions.answer_c: With other amateur stations and stations of the authorities and organisations with security tasks (BOS)
questions.answer_d: With other amateur stations and stations of the aeronautical and/or maritime mobile service

questions.question: What applies to radio amateurs with regard to frequency use? With the amateur station, a radio amateur may ...
questions.answer_a: transmit on the frequencies designated for the amateur service.
questions.answer_b: transmit on all frequencies permitted for the radio amateur's ITU region.
questions.answer_c: use any frequencies, provided no other radiocommunication services suffer interference.
questions.answer_d: also transmit on frequencies not designated for the amateur service in the course of an emergency communications exercise.

questions.question: What right do radio amateurs have with regard to operating transmitting equipment? A radio amateur ...
questions.answer_a: is entitled to operate transmitting equipment that is commercially available, home-built or converted to amateur frequencies.
questions.answer_b: never needs a site certificate from the BNetzA for the amateur station.
questions.answer_c: need not observe the relevant BNetzA provisions on electrical safety.
questions.answer_d: may at any time use the amateur station to transmit messages that do not concern the amateur service on behalf of and to third parties.

questions.question: Under the Amateur Radio Act (Amateurfunkgesetz, AFuG), is a minimum age required for the issue of an amateur radio licence?
questions.answer_a: The Amateur Radio Act (Amateurfunkgesetz, AFuG) does not provide for a minimum age.
questions.answer_b: The minimum age for applying is 15 years.
questions.answer_c: From Class E upwards, the Amateur Radio Act (Amateurfunkgesetz, AFuG) provides for a minimum age of 16 years.
questions.answer_d: Having reached the age of majority is a prerequisite for the issue of Class A.

questions.question: May a radio amateur temporarily transfer the amateur radio licence to another person? The amateur radio licence is ...
questions.answer_a: tied to the person named in the licence document and is not transferable.
questions.answer_b: transferable to persons in the same household after prior notification to the Federal Network Agency (BNetzA).
questions.answer_c: transferable if the person is a radio amateur who has successfully passed the examination.
questions.answer_d: transferable if the persons concerned are foreign radio amateurs staying temporarily in Germany.

questions.question: Apart from having passed the amateur radio examination, what is absolutely necessary for you to be allowed to operate an amateur station?
questions.answer_a: An authorisation to participate in the amateur service
questions.answer_b: Submission of proof that the antenna installation has been professionally installed
questions.answer_c: Obtaining an EMVU certificate from the competent authority
questions.answer_d: Submission of calculation documents and supplementary measurement reports for the worst-case configuration of the antenna installation

questions.question: Which of the following documents do you need to be a radio amateur within the meaning of the Amateur Radio Act (Amateurfunkgesetz, AFuG)?
questions.answer_a: An amateur radio certificate or a harmonised amateur radio examination certificate
questions.answer_b: A certificate of good conduct showing that you have no criminal record
questions.answer_c: A valid identity card or passport showing that you are resident in the Federal Republic
questions.answer_d: A certificate stating that you have successfully taken part in training operation in the Federal Republic of Germany

questions.question: Which German authority performs the tasks and exercises the powers arising from the Amateur Radio Act (Amateurfunkgesetz, AFuG) and the Amateur Radio Ordinance (Amateurfunkverordnung, AFuV)?
questions.answer_c: The Federal Institution for Posts and Telecommunications (Bundesanstalt für Post und Telekommunikation)
questions.answer_d: The Federal Agency for Public Safety Digital Radio (Bundesanstalt für den Digitalfunk der BOS)

questions.question: Under the Amateur Radio Act (Amateurfunkgesetz, AFuG), an amateur station is a station that consists of ...
questions.answer_a: one or more transmitters and receivers, including the antenna installations and the accessory equipment necessary for their operation, and that can be operated on at least one of the frequencies designated for the amateur service in the Frequency Plan.
questions.answer_b: several transmitters and receivers and that can be operated on at least three of the frequencies designated for the amateur service in the Frequency Plan above 30 MHz.
questions.answer_c: several transmitters and receivers and that can be operated on at least three of the frequencies designated for the amateur service in the Frequency Plan below 30 MHz.
questions.answer_d: a receiver, including the antenna installations and the accessory equipment necessary for its operation, and that can be operated on at least one of the frequencies designated for the amateur service in the Frequency Plan.

questions.question: Within the meaning of the Amateur Radio Act (Amateurfunkgesetz, AFuG), the amateur service is a radiocommunication service that ...
questions.answer_a: is carried on by radio amateurs among themselves, for experimental and technical-scientific studies, for their own further education, for international understanding and for supporting relief operations in emergencies and disasters.
questions.answer_b: enjoys priority over other radiocommunication services on all frequencies designated in the Frequency Plan and may be carried on to support relief operations in emergencies and disasters.
questions.answer_c: may be carried on by radio amateurs with radio equipment specially approved for it, on all frequencies designated in the Frequency Plan and for their own further education.
questions.answer_d: is carried on by radio amateurs out of personal interest, out of commercial interests and for technical studies.

questions.question: Which law forms the legal basis for, and lays down the requirements and conditions for, participation in the amateur service in Germany?
questions.answer_c: The Act on Making Radio Equipment Available on the Market
questions.answer_d: The Act on the Electromagnetic Compatibility of Equipment

questions.question: How is the term "beacon" defined according to the wording of the Amateur Radio Ordinance (Amateurfunkverordnung, AFuV)?
questions.answer_a: A "beacon" is an automatically operating amateur radio transmitter (also in satellites) that automatically produces continuously repeated transmissions for observing field strength or for reception tests.
questions.answer_b: A "beacon" is an automatically operating amateur radio transmitter (also in satellites) that automatically produces continuously repeated transmissions for position fixing on the high seas.
questions.answer_c: A "beacon" is an amateur radio transmitter that produces continuously repeated transmissions for position fixing in emergencies and disasters.
questions.answer_d: A "beacon" is an amateur radio transmitter that transmits continuously repeated signals to identify the HF band edges.

questions.question: How is the term "repeater" defined according to the wording of the Amateur Radio Ordinance (Amateurfunkverordnung, AFuV)?
questions.answer_a: A "repeater" is a remotely controlled or automatically operating amateur station, or a remotely controlled and automatically operating amateur station in satellites, that retransmits or forwards, when triggered remotely, received amateur radio transmissions, parts of them or other content fed in or stored.
questions.answer_b: A "repeater" is an amateur station permanently attended by a radio amateur that transmits, when triggered remotely, received amateur radio transmissions, parts of them or other signals fed in or stored, and thereby serves to make amateur stations easier to reach.
questions.answer_c: A "repeater" is a remotely controlled amateur station that is operated with the personal call sign of its holder.
questions.answer_d: A "repeater" is a remotely controlled amateur station that may only be operated at a geographically exposed location.

questions.question: How is the term "club station" defined according to the wording of the Amateur Radio Ordinance (Amateurfunkverordnung, AFuV)?
questions.answer_a: A "club station" is an amateur station operated by at least three members of a group of radio amateurs using a jointly used call sign.
questions.answer_b: A "club station" is an amateur station operated by at least four members of a group of radio amateurs using their personal call signs.
questions.answer_c: A "club station" is an amateur station operated at a geographically exposed location.
questions.answer_d: A "club station" is an amateur station that may only be operated by a registered association.

questions.question: For which purposes are assignments with exceptions to the technical and operating conditions of the Amateur Radio Ordinance (Amateurfunkverordnung, AFuV) possible?
questions.answer_a: For special experimental and technical-scientific studies with an amateur station
questions.answer_b: For exercises in handling radio communication in emergencies and disasters
questions.answer_c: For alignment work and measurements on transmitters without a termination
questions.answer_d: For the use of additional frequency ranges that are not designated for the amateur service in the Frequency Usage Plan

questions.question: Is a special permit from the Federal Network Agency (BNetzA) required to operate an amateur station on board a vessel or an aircraft?
questions.answer_b: If the radio amateur also holds an aeronautical or maritime radio operator's certificate, no special permit is needed.
questions.answer_c: A special permit is required in every case.
questions.answer_d: A special permit is required for radiated powers of more than 10 W EIRP.

questions.question: Which data on the holder of a personal call sign are included in the call sign list published by the Federal Network Agency (BNetzA)?
questions.answer_a: Name, call sign and, unless the holder has objected, the address
questions.answer_b: Name, call sign and the e-mail address
questions.answer_c: Name, call sign and the telephone number
questions.answer_d: Name, call sign and, unless the holder has objected, the date of birth

questions.question: Within what period must the holder of an amateur radio licence notify the BNetzA in writing or electronically of a change of name or address, even if the holder does not own, set up or operate an amateur station?
questions.answer_d: At least 14 days before the change

questions.question: Under what condition is it permitted to transmit an unmodulated or unkeyed carrier?
questions.answer_a: If it is brief, e.g. for tuning
questions.answer_b: Provided it is a digital signal
questions.answer_c: If propagation conditions do not allow long-distance contacts
questions.answer_d: Provided the transmit power is reduced to below 1 W

questions.question: What must be observed with regard to emissions during alignment work and measurements on transmitters?
questions.answer_a: Suitable measures must be taken that effectively prevent the unrestricted radiation of signals.
questions.answer_b: The transmitter case must not be opened.
questions.answer_c: The antenna cable must be firmly connected.
questions.answer_d: Transmissions may only be made at half power.

questions.question: What does the Amateur Radio Ordinance (Amateurfunkverordnung, AFuV) say about unwanted emissions?
questions.answer_a: Unwanted emissions must be kept to the lowest possible level.
questions.answer_b: Unwanted emissions must be limited to 60 dB relative to the wanted signal.
questions.answer_c: Unwanted emissions must be limited to 40 dB relative to the wanted signal.

questions.question: When must a radio amateur keep a written record of the operation of the amateur station, e.g. as a log?
questions.answer_a: At the request of the Federal Network Agency (BNetzA)
questions.answer_d: In the first 12 months after being licensed

questions.question: For what purposes can the Federal Network Agency (BNetzA) require written records of radio operation?
questions.answer_a: To investigate causes of interference or to clarify questions of frequency engineering
questions.answer_b: To check the radio amateur's qualification and the content of the transmissions
questions.answer_c: As proof of compliance with limits under the Federal Immission Control Act (BImSchG)
questions.answer_d: As proof for billing the frequency usage contributions

questions.question: In which case must a radio amateur submit technical documentation on the transmitting equipment to the Federal Network Agency (BNetzA) under the Amateur Radio Ordinance (Amateurfunkverordnung, AFuV)?
questions.answer_a: At the request of the Federal Network Agency (BNetzA)
questions.answer_b: With every technical modification to the transmitting equipment
questions.answer_c: Without delay after receiving the amateur radio licence
questions.answer_d: With transmit powers greater than 750 W

questions.question: Which technical requirements, among others, does the Amateur Radio Ordinance (Amateurfunkverordnung, AFuV) impose on an amateur station?
questions.answer_a: It must be set up and maintained in accordance with the generally accepted rules of engineering.
questions.answer_b: All equipment needed for transmitting must carry a CE mark.
questions.answer_c: The transmit signal must be fed to the antenna through a coaxial cable.
questions.answer_d: By design, it must not be able to produce more power than its owner is permitted to use.

questions.question: May international distress, urgency and safety signals (e.g. MAYDAY, PAN PAN, SÉCURITÉ) be transmitted in amateur radio communication?
questions.answer_a: The use of these signals is expressly prohibited.
questions.answer_b: Amateur stations near the coast are permitted to transmit these signals.
questions.answer_c: In an emergency, the signals may be transmitted.
questions.answer_d: The use of these signals is permitted on the HF bands.

questions.question: Under the AFuV, which content of amateur radio communication may be encrypted for the purpose of obscuring its meaning?
questions.answer_a: Control signals for satellites, for remotely controlled and automatically operating stations and for remote operation
questions.answer_b: Control signals for satellites, confidential information and messages of a personal character
questions.answer_c: Content that is digitally encoded because of the transmission method used
questions.answer_d: Content concerning technical matters of the amateur service that are worth protecting

questions.question: Only plain language may be used in amateur radio communication. What does <u>not</u> count as plain language and is therefore not permitted?
questions.answer_a: Voice encryption to obscure the content
questions.answer_b: Q codes and amateur radio abbreviations
questions.answer_c: Digital modes that need a decoder

questions.question: What applies to the reception of amateur radio transmissions?
questions.answer_a: No authorisation to participate in the amateur service is required.
questions.answer_b: Only receivers approved under the TKG may be used.
questions.answer_c: A listener call sign from the "DE series" must be assigned.
questions.answer_d: Recognition as an "SWL" is required, together with membership of an amateur radio society.

questions.question: Where can radio amateurs look up which frequency ranges they may use in Germany according to their certificate class?
questions.answer_a: In Annex 1 to the Amateur Radio Ordinance (Amateurfunkverordnung, AFuV) and, where applicable, further notices of the BNetzA
questions.answer_c: In the Amateur Radio Act (Amateurfunkgesetz, AFuG)
questions.answer_d: In the Annex to the Frequency Ordinance (FreqV) and the associated notices of the BNetzA

questions.question: Is a radio amateur entitled to the assignment of a particular call sign?
questions.answer_a: No, there is no such entitlement.
questions.answer_b: Yes, if it has not yet been assigned.
questions.answer_c: No, unless special personal reasons can be shown and the call sign is free.
questions.answer_d: Yes, if it has already been assigned to the same radio amateur before.

questions.question: How can an amateur station be recognised on the air?
questions.answer_c: By the class of emission used

questions.question: Under Order 13/2005, which phonetic alphabet must be used when giving the call sign to identify an amateur station?
questions.answer_a: The international phonetic alphabet according to the Radio Regulations (Appendix 14)
questions.answer_c: The English phonetic alphabet of the ITU conference in Madrid of 1932
questions.answer_d: The German phonetic alphabet according to DIN 5009

questions.question: When must a radio amateur give the call sign?
questions.answer_a: At the beginning and end of every contact and at least every 10 minutes
questions.answer_b: When requested by another station taking part in the communication
questions.answer_c: At least every 15 minutes during a contact
questions.answer_d: No later than 5 minutes after an uninterrupted transmission

questions.question: Why is "DL250BTHVN" a permissible German amateur call sign?
questions.answer_a: Because, for special general occasions, the Call Sign Plan also provides for call signs with a suffix of up to 7 characters, which may contain digits and ends with a letter.
questions.answer_b: Because personal call signs to which the Call Sign Plan does not apply are also issued to radio amateurs of particular merit.
questions.answer_c: Because special call signs with at least 3 digits are issued to certain public bodies, such as arts and cultural institutions.
questions.answer_d: Because this was laid down in a special order of the Federal Network Agency (BNetzA) on account of a special historical occasion with international effect.

questions.question: How are personal German amateur call signs formed? They consist of ...
questions.answer_a: a 2-letter prefix (country identifier), one digit and a 2- or 3-letter suffix.
questions.answer_b: a 2-letter suffix (country identifier), two digits and a 2- or 3-letter prefix.
questions.answer_c: a 1-letter prefix (country identifier), one or two digits and a 1-, 2- or 3-letter suffix.
questions.answer_d: a 2-letter suffix (country identifier), one digit and a 1-, 2- or 3-letter prefix.

questions.question: Which categories of call sign assignment exist in amateur radio, among others?
questions.answer_a: Personal call signs, call signs for remotely controlled and automatically operating amateur stations, club station call signs
questions.answer_b: Personal call signs, family call signs, club station call signs
questions.answer_c: Personal call signs, club station call signs, contest call signs
questions.answer_d: Personal call signs, call signs for remotely controlled and automatically operating amateur stations, mobile radio call signs

questions.question: In which set of rules can the requirements for forming call signs for the amateur service in Germany be found?
questions.answer_a: In the Call Sign Plan of the Federal Network Agency (BNetzA)
questions.answer_b: In the Amateur Radio Act (Amateurfunkgesetz, AFuG)
questions.answer_d: In the Radio Regulations (RR) of the ITU

questions.question: By whom must the call sign suffix "/T" or "/Trainee" be used during training operation?
questions.answer_c: By the trainee and the instructor
questions.answer_d: By the person responsible for the school station

questions.question: What must be observed when carrying out training operation?
questions.answer_a: At the request of the Federal Network Agency (BNetzA), the instructor must provide information on the type and scope of the training operation.
questions.answer_b: During training operation, taking part in amateur radio contests is not permitted.
questions.answer_c: Training operation may only be carried out in the presence of the instructor at a club or school station.
questions.answer_d: Training operation may only be carried out in telephony (SSB or FM).

questions.question: What must, among other things, be observed when carrying out training operation? Training operation may ...
questions.answer_a: only be carried out within the scope of privileges of the instructor's call sign assignment.
questions.answer_b: not be carried out in Morse telegraphy.
questions.answer_c: only be carried out with a maximum radiated power of 10 W EIRP.
questions.answer_d: only be carried out at a club station.

questions.question: Persons who are not radio amateurs may take part in training operation ...
questions.answer_a: only under the direct guidance and supervision of a radio amateur with an assigned Class A or E call sign.
questions.answer_b: only at club stations under the supervision of a radio amateur with an assigned Class A or E call sign.
questions.answer_c: at weekends as well, without any special conditions.
questions.answer_d: even without the guidance and supervision of the instructing radio amateur.

questions.question: Under the Amateur Radio Ordinance (Amateurfunkverordnung, AFuV), on what condition may a radio amateur carry out training operation?
questions.answer_a: As the holder of a Class A or E authorisation to participate in the amateur service
questions.answer_b: Only as the holder of a Class A authorisation to participate in the amateur service
questions.answer_c: Only after holding an authorisation to participate in the amateur service for at least 1 year
questions.answer_d: As the holder of a valid assignment of a training call sign

questions.question: What purpose does training operation serve under the Amateur Radio Ordinance (Amateurfunkverordnung, AFuV)? It is intended for ...
questions.answer_a: practical preparation for taking the examination of competence to obtain an amateur radio certificate.
questions.answer_b: the sole purpose of demonstrating amateur radio operation.
questions.answer_c: the trainee's participation in the amateur service without supervision.
questions.answer_d: perfecting the radio amateur's skills in Morse telegraphy.

questions.question: Which statement is correct regarding a change of location of a club station?
questions.answer_a: Short-term changes of location need not be notified to the BNetzA.
questions.answer_b: Changes of location are not permitted for club stations.
questions.answer_c: Short-term changes of location must be notified to the BNetzA.
questions.answer_d: As a rule, changes of location need not be notified to the BNetzA.

questions.question: Which of the following radio amateurs may operate a Class A club station on the 40 m amateur band?
questions.answer_a: Holders of a Class A amateur radio licence
questions.answer_b: Holders of a Class E amateur radio licence
questions.answer_c: Holders of a Class N amateur radio licence
questions.answer_d: Holders of an amateur radio licence of any class

questions.question: You are using a club station call sign and hold an amateur radio certificate of a different class from that of the club station's assignment. On which frequency ranges and with what power may you transmit? According to the scope of privileges ...
questions.answer_a: of the lower of the two classes.
questions.answer_b: of the higher of the two classes.
questions.answer_c: of the class of my personal licence.
questions.answer_d: of the class of the club station.

questions.question: Under the provisions of the Amateur Radio Ordinance (Amateurfunkverordnung, AFuV), may a radio amateur with an authorisation to participate in the amateur service operate with the club station's call sign without being a member of the group operating it?
questions.answer_a: Non-members may also operate at club stations.
questions.answer_b: Only the members of the group may operate the club station.
questions.answer_c: Operation must take place in the presence of a member of the group.
questions.answer_d: The radio amateur must notify the BNetzA of this at least two days beforehand.

questions.question: What is needed for a radio amateur to be allowed to share the call sign of a club station?
questions.answer_a: The radio amateur must hold an authorisation to participate in the amateur service.
questions.answer_b: The radio amateur must be a member of the group of radio amateurs that operates the club station.
questions.answer_c: The radio amateur must have an amateur radio certificate that corresponds to the class of the club station.
questions.answer_d: The radio amateur must hold a call sign of the highest amateur radio class.

questions.question: Under the Amateur Radio Act (Amateurfunkgesetz, AFuG), from when may a radio amateur operate a club station?
questions.answer_a: After having personally received an authorisation for the amateur service and the assignment of a club station call sign
questions.answer_b: Only 3 months after passing the amateur radio examination and the assignment of a club station call sign
questions.answer_c: Operation may take place on presentation of a harmonised examination certificate
questions.answer_d: Only after the BNetzA has checked the location and a club station call sign has been assigned

questions.question: What requirement must be met for a call sign to be issued for operating a club station?
questions.answer_a: An authorisation to participate in the amateur service under Section 3(1) AFuG.
questions.answer_b: The radio amateur responsible for the club station must in every case be the operator of an automatically operating station.
questions.answer_c: The radio amateur responsible for the club station must in every case hold a call sign of the highest amateur radio class.
questions.answer_d: A HAREC certificate or an amateur radio certificate

questions.question: What requirements must be met for a call sign to be issued for operating a club station?
questions.answer_a: The assignment of a call sign for operating a club station depends on the leader of a group of radio amateurs naming the responsible radio amateur.
questions.answer_b: The radio amateur responsible for the club station must in every case hold a call sign of the highest amateur radio class.
questions.answer_c: The responsible radio amateur must have held an amateur radio certificate for at least 2 years.
questions.answer_d: The leader of an amateur radio society constituted as a registered association (e. V.) must also be the radio amateur responsible for the club station applied for.

questions.question: When may the radio amateur responsible for a repeater exclude a particular radio amateur from operating through it?
questions.answer_a: If this serves to ensure interference-free operation of the repeater
questions.answer_b: If a radio amateur uses the repeater too often
questions.answer_c: If the repeater usage fee has not been paid
questions.answer_d: If a radio amateur has not yet reached the minimum age

questions.question: What is the maximum permitted radiated power of a repeater above 30 MHz?
questions.answer_b: 750 W PEP for Class A, 75 W PEP for Class E and 10 W PEP for Class N

questions.question: Under what conditions may a radio amateur operate an amateur station as a repeater?
questions.answer_a: If a call sign has been assigned to the radio amateur for the repeater and the conditions laid down in the assignment are met
questions.answer_b: If the repeater does not have a long range
questions.answer_c: If at least 20 signatures can be presented as proof of need and the conditions for repeaters are met
